Resolves #18313
Related: #18303, #18314, #18315, #18316

A Group-owned placement participant records settled popup movement as relative offsets. Main-window movement rebases current hints without adding history or moving popups. Undo/redo commits the hint first, moves the exact native generation, and retains the observed outcome separately.

Both hosts acquire one placement owner per Group. Workstation now saves live hints, seeds saved hints after all workspace documents register, and enables the existing geometry stream when a restored window mounts or reloads. Its native position is then restored through the placement owner. `WorkspaceSet` excludes auxiliary participants from document operations; diagnostics retain the full snapshot while listing only document keys. `Transaction.retireGroup` owns the single retirement event.

Rebased onto the merged ownership-admission change at `dev@1182a7cf11`. The placement implementation patches are preserved; conflicts were the measured host baselines and an inherited test comment.

The [ticket's producer boundary](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18313) assigns placement to registered semantic workspace documents. The all-origin migration owns full-Workspace birth and its first shared-history write; the final Workstation journey proves the composition. All seven placement ACs remain required.

Evidence: L3 (real Chrome popup geometry, SharedWorker state through Neural Link, IndexedDB save and fresh cold boot) → L3 required (native movement and causal undo/redo). Refusal, clamp, missing-screen, N-popup and retired-generation controls are L2. Residual: ordinary Workstation tear-out document admission and the final all-origin journey; Residual-Owner: #18314, #18316.

## Deltas from ticket

The [document-bearing-slot boundary](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18313) follows the wire contract: every hint key must name a workspace document. An ordinary bare vessel has no such document yet. Placement creates no second document owner.

Incidental CI cleanup: the existing destroy-sentinel spec now registers its fixture class once and injects the failure per instance. Repeated cases no longer collide in the same worker; the engine namespace guard and recovery assertions are unchanged.

`preserve` now permits a current-state rebase with existing history while retaining row identity and the redo tail. The native coordinator uses the existing buffer instead of its bespoke settle timer. Tagged geometry publication advances the polling baseline, preventing an untagged echo.

Decision Record impact: ADR 0029 documents observed relative placement, main-frame rebasing and correlated native outcomes.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** `applyHint` fires `Transaction.fire('effectReceipt', …)` unconditionally, including on the `!live()` path — the *store* is fenced (`if (live()) me.#receipts.set(…)`, covered by `a native completion from a retired binding cannot update the successor receipt`) but the *event* still reaches listeners carrying a `workspaceKey` whose binding has already been replaced. I grepped it: two emitters (here and `transaction/Commit.mjs:182`), **zero production consumers** — the only listener is `TransactionAtomic.spec.mjs:279` (positive control: the same grep finds the emitter at `Placement.mjs:341`, so the null is a real null). So this is inert today and I am not asking for a code change. It stops being inert in **#18316**, which is where a save/reload/undo journey would plausibly add the first real listener; a consumer that keys on `workspaceKey` without reading `status` would act on a superseded generation. One sentence on the event contract — *consumers must gate on `status`; a `stale` receipt names a binding that no longer exists* — is worth carrying into whichever PR adds the first consumer. I will raise it there rather than hold this one.

**Documented search — the two defects I went looking for and could not substantiate.** Recording both, because the reasoning is the durable part and the next reader of this file will form the same two hypotheses I did:

1. **"The feature is inert in production."** `mainBindingKey` defaults to `'main'` and *neither* caller overrides it (`Workspace.mjs:956`, `DemoBWorkspace.mjs:163` pass only `mainWorkspaceKey`), while `MAIN_WORKSPACE_ID` is `'workstation-main'` / `'demo-b-main'`. If bindings were keyed by document id, `group.bindings.get('main')` would be `undefined`, `observedHints()` would always return `{}` and every `ingest()` would return `null` — unit-green, product-dead. **Falsified by `DockPlacementNL.spec.mjs`**, which drives the real `crossWindow` app through real CDP window movement and reads a real `hints['demo-b-popup'].dx`. That value cannot exist unless the main rect resolved. The main *window* genuinely binds under the reserved key `'main'`; popup bindings reuse their document key. Two namespaces, intentionally.
2. **"The AC-6 guard is pointed at the wrong key."** Given namespace (1), `prepare()`'s `Object.hasOwn(topology.placementHints, this.mainWorkspaceKey)` checks `'workstation-main'`, while a hint naming the main *slot* in the bindings namespace would be keyed `'main'` — so the guard looked unable to fire for the case it names, leaving `initialHints` from a persisted envelope as an unguarded path (and `project()` would then hand `'main'` to `applyHint`, physically moving the main frame). **Falsified by `Persistence.mjs:580`**: `if (!Object.hasOwn(topology.workspaces || {}, workspaceKey))` rejects any hint key that is not a workspace document, and `prepare()` throws on the returned errors. A `'main'`-keyed hint dies at the wire contract; the `mainWorkspaceKey` guard then covers the *only* residue the wire contract cannot see — a hint keyed by the main workspace's own document id, which is a legitimate workspace and would otherwise validate clean. Both checks are correctly aimed, and `prepare({'workstation-main': …}) → throws` is the right positive control for the second.

I also looked for, and did not find: a rect, screen coordinate or `windowId` reachable into the durable envelope (the e2e asserts the negative against the *saved* collection, not the in-memory hints — that is the stronger placement); a path where the burst's `generation` stamp is read after the flush rather than captured before it; and a window-granular suppression flag (the marker is pushed and `finally`-popped around one `await`, and `WindowPosition.mjs:178` advances the poll baseline while it is still live precisely so the untagged echo cannot outlive it).
